items.title: Laser Focus at the Top of the World
items.snippet: A next-generation geodetic instrument developed by NASA, part of a network that helps measure satellites’ orbits and the planet’s shape, has debuted in Svalbard, Norway.

items.title: Watch live today: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
items.snippet: An Ariane 6 rocket will launch 36 Amazon broadband satellites to orbit early on Nov. 23, just eight days after a ULA Vulcan Centaur failed during its mission for Amazon. Watch it live here.

items.title: Impossible volcanic eruption spotted in deepest part of the ocean, perplexing scientists
items.snippet: Scientists are perplexed at discovering the world's deepest explosive volcanic eruption at Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench.

items.title: A 194-year-old tortoise has a remarkable anti-aging secret hidden in its DNA
items.snippet: At an astonishing 194 years old, Jonathan the giant tortoise is the world's oldest living land animal, and scientists may have finally uncovered the secrets behind his extraordinary lifespan. Researchers identified 287 unique genetic variants linked to processes that help repair damaged DNA, control inflammation, regulate insulin, and suppress cancer.

items.title: DNA’s secret sunscreen may have helped life survive on early Earth
items.snippet: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why early life may have survived Earth's intense ultraviolet radiation: a key component of DNA appears to turn potentially destructive damage into something easier to repair. The discovery could help solve a decades-old evolutionary mystery and reveal how life endured the harsh conditions of our planet's earliest days.

items.title: A mysterious gap hints at black holes born from stars that never exploded
items.snippet: Massive stars may be quietly collapsing into black holes without ever producing the spectacular supernova explosions scientists typically expect. A surprising pattern in 257 black hole mergers suggests these mysterious stellar disappearances could explain the origins of a large population of black holes throughout the universe.

items.snippet: A surprising discovery at Brown University is challenging one of chemistry's most fundamental textbook explanations. items.snippet: Medications taken years or even long ago may leave lasting changes in your gut microbiome, according to a study of more than 2,500 people. items.title: Interstellar solar sails hit a bizarre problem at 75% of light speed
items.snippet: Scientists have discovered a surprising obstacle to interstellar travel: at extreme speeds, the light propelling futuristic solar sails could actually begin slowing them down. Once a spacecraft reaches 75% of the speed of light, some scattered light starts producing drag, potentially complicating humanity’s plans to reach distant stars.

items.title: Reliance on technology is eroding trust in one another and ability to tell what is even real, expert warns
items.snippet: The danger of generative AI is not some distant algorithmic failure; it is the slow erosion of our ability to tell what's real, to trust our institutions and to think for ourselves at all. These are the warnings of Mateusz Łabuz in his new book, The End of Reality.
